intro.say: Solid shapes are shapes you can hold, like a ball or a box!

rounds.say: A cube is like a dice. It has flat square faces, all the same size.
rounds.caption: cube

rounds.say: A sphere is round like a ball. It has no flat faces and no corners.
rounds.caption: sphere

rounds.say: A cone has a round bottom and a pointy top, like an ice cream cone. A cylinder is like a can.
rounds.caption: cone · cylinder

options.label: dice
options.why: A dice is a cube. It has flat faces.

options.label: can
options.why: A can is a cylinder.

rounds.explain: A ball is a sphere, round all over.

options.label: cone
options.why: That is a cone, with a pointy top.

options.label: can
options.why: That is a cylinder, like a tube.

rounds.explain: A dice is a cube, with square faces all the same.

rounds.ask: What solid shape is this can?

options.label: sphere
options.why: A sphere is round all over, like a ball.

options.label: cone
options.why: A cone has a pointy top.

rounds.explain: A can is a cylinder, with two round ends and a curved side.

rounds.ask: Which shape has a pointy top?

options.label: cylinder
options.why: A cylinder has two flat ends.

options.label: sphere
options.why: A sphere is round all over.

rounds.explain: A cone comes to a point at the top.

rounds.ask: Is it a sphere or a cube? Sort them!
rounds.explain: Round things are spheres, and box shapes with equal square faces are cubes.

intro.say: Some solid shapes roll and some stack. Let's find out why!

rounds.say: A sphere is curved all over, so it rolls any way you push it.
rounds.caption: rolls

rounds.say: A cuboid is shaped like a box. Its faces are flat, so boxes stack into a tall tower.
rounds.caption: cuboid · stacks

rounds.say: A cylinder has flat ends and a curved side. Stand it up to stack, or lay it down to roll!
rounds.caption: stacks and rolls

options.label: dice
options.why: A dice tumbles but does not roll smoothly.

options.label: box
options.why: A box has flat faces, so it slides.

rounds.explain: A ball is a sphere, curved all over, so it rolls easily.

rounds.ask: Which shape is best for building a tall tower?

options.label: ball
options.why: Balls roll off each other.

options.label: cone
options.why: A pointy top is hard to stack on.

rounds.explain: Cubes have flat faces, so they sit safely on top of each other.

rounds.ask: Does it roll or stack? Sort them!
rounds.explain: Round things roll. Things with flat faces stack.

rounds.ask: A dice is a cube. How many flat faces does it have?

options.why: 8 is how many corners it has. Count the faces.
Count the top and bottom too.

rounds.explain: A cube has 6 faces: top, bottom and four sides.
rounds.hint: Count top, bottom, front, back and two sides.

rounds.ask: Which one is a cuboid, like a long box?

options.label: can
options.why: A can is a cylinder.

options.label: ball
options.why: A ball is a sphere.

rounds.explain: A box is a cuboid, with six flat faces shaped like rectangles.

rounds.ask: Which shape can roll AND stack?

options.label: dice
options.why: A dice stacks but won't roll.

options.label: ball
options.why: A ball rolls but won't stack.

rounds.explain: A cylinder stacks on its flat ends and rolls on its curved side.

intro.say: Let's count faces, corners and edges, and solve solid shape riddles!

rounds.say: A cuboid has 6 flat faces, 8 corners and 12 edges. An edge is where two faces meet.
rounds.caption: 6 faces · 8 corners · 12 edges

rounds.say: A cylinder has 2 flat faces shaped like circles, and one curved side. It has no corners.
rounds.caption: 2 circle faces · no corners

rounds.ask: I have one flat circle face, a curved side and a point. What am I?

options.label: cylinder
options.why: A cylinder has two flat ends and no point.

options.label: sphere
options.why: A sphere has no flat face at all.

rounds.explain: A cone has one circle face and comes to a point.

rounds.ask: How many corners does a cube have?

options.why: That is just the top. Count the bottom too.
6 is the number of faces. Count the pointy corners.

rounds.explain: A cube has 4 corners on top and 4 on the bottom, 8 in all.

rounds.ask: You dip the flat end of a can in paint and stamp it. What shape do you see?

options.why: A can's end is round.
A can's end has no corners.

rounds.explain: The flat end of a cylinder is a circle.

rounds.ask: Now you stamp one face of a dice. What shape do you see?

options.why: A dice face has straight sides.
A dice face has 4 sides.

rounds.explain: Every face of a cube is a square.

rounds.ask: Which shape has the most flat faces?

options.label: cone
options.why: A cone has just 1 flat face.

options.label: cylinder
options.why: A cylinder has only 2 flat faces.

rounds.explain: A cube has 6 flat faces, more than a cylinder or a cone.

rounds.ask: Does it have corners or no corners?
rounds.explain: Cubes and cuboids have corners. Spheres and cylinders have none.
